subject: SparrowPay inference deep-dive recap & next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@sparrowpay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@sparrowpay.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: SparrowPay discovery recap — latency/throughput focus

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we stay aligned. Short version: SparrowPay's top priorities are (1) sub-150ms P95 text-inference latency for short payment-authoring requests (~64 tokens), (2) predictable burst handling at end-of-day settlement (~3x baseline traffic for 10-15 minutes), and (3) strict data isolation and auditability for payments data.

Pain points you called out:
- Current inference stack sees 300–450ms P95 for your current LLM path, which hurts conversion in UX flows.
- Spiky traffic at 02:00 UTC causes failed calls and retries due to autoscaling noise.
- Security team requires audit logs and a deploy topology that keeps customer data on a private VPC.

Hypothesis (what Redwood can do):
- Short, latency-optimized endpoints backed by a quantized model variant for production critical flows.
- Reserved/Dedicated capacity for your peak windows plus autoscale-on-burst with warm standby nodes.
- VPC/private deployment with KMS-integrated keys and request-level audit logs.

Technical notes from the call (items for engineering follow-up):
- Target SLO: P95 <= 150ms for requests <= 64 tokens (scoping for 256-token tail also needed).
- Baseline throughput: 120 reqs/sec sustained in US-East, burst to 360 reqs/sec for 10-15 minutes.
- Concurrency goal: keep tail latency predictable at 8–12 concurrent requests per replica.
- Model preference: open to 30–70B family; prioritize a quantized fp16/qlora-like variant for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: I attached the traffic sample you shared (sparrow-traffic-sample.csv) and flagged your current arch diagram.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Connor & Karthik to review the traffic sample and provide a sizing sketch (ETA: 48 hours).
2) Hawkish plan for a private-demo in our VPC staging using a quantized variant (schedule week of Feb 20).
3) Security questionnaire + evidence pack request (we can start collecting SOC2 items while we size).

Action owners: Connor (sizing sketch), Karthik (quantization/throughput recommendation), Hannah (security + scheduling).

Thanks — will follow up with a short technical note once Connor has the initial sizing.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: sparrow-traffic-sample.csv (csv), current-arch-diagram.png (image)
From: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@sparrowpay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sparrowpay.com>, infra@sparrowpay.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SparrowPay discovery recap — latency/throughput focus

Thanks Hannah — that matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications:
- The 120 reqs/sec baseline is per region (primarily us-east) — we currently have a small presence in eu-west for redundancy but traffic is <10% there.
- Typical request sizes: 60% are <= 64 tokens, 30% are 65–256, and 10% are >256 (rare long-form debugging flows).
- Burst pattern: daily end-of-day settlement between 02:00–02:20 UTC; we need zero-downtime for that window.

Two asks before the deep-demo:
1) Can you sketch an architecture that shows a private deployment with reserved capacity + burst nodes (how many warm nodes vs cold scale)?
2) Any early quantization guidance — we want to understand quality delta if we move to a 4-bit/8-bit variant for the short endpoints.

I'll loop in our infra folks on the scheduling. Priya — can you share your SOC2 evidence timeline so we can align?

- Liam
Liam O'Neil
Head of Platform Engineering, SparrowPay
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@sparrowpay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@sparrowpay.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SparrowPay discovery recap — latency/throughput focus

Liam / Priya — quick technical follow-up from our infra team. See inline answers and a proposed sizing sketch below.

Inline:
- Region: We'll size primary pool in us-east. EU presence can be handled by smaller dedicated pool (10% of us-east capacity) or routed to hosted fallback depending on cost tolerance.
- Request mix: good detail — we'll treat <=64 token as primary latency-critical SLA.

Sizing sketch (initial, conservative):
- Baseline target (us-east): sustain 120 reqs/sec with P95 <= 150ms for <=64 tokens.
- Replica perf estimate (quantized 30B fp16-ish variant): ~15–20 reqs/sec at P95 <= 150ms with concurrency 10 (on mid-range A100/A10x-equivalent).
- Baseline pool: 8 replicas (handles ~160 reqs/sec headroom).
- Burst plan: keep 3 warm standby replicas (cold start < 90s, warm < 8s). For 3x burst to 360 reqs/sec, autoscale adds 10 replicas (total 18) within targeted burst window if warm nodes pre-warmed to KV prefixes and container images.
- Can reduce replica count by using larger instance types or higher-performance GPUs; we can provide cost delta.

Quantization & quality guidance (preliminary):
- 8-bit quant (Q8) typically preserves >98% of output quality for instruction-following classification/regression tasks; 4-bit aggressive quant (Q4/QLoRA-style) can introduce subtle tokenization/fluency regressions on some prompts.
- Recommendation: 2-tier model family — Q8 for the core latency-critical endpoints, Q4 candidate for low-cost batch/offline flows (or fallback when cost pressure > 40% of spend).

Security / topology notes:
- Private deployment: Redwood Private with VPC peering + customer-managed NAT. We support HSM/KMS for keys and request-level audit logs shipped to your SIEM via secure connector.
- Audit logs retention policy can be configured per retention class (30/90/365 days) and exported via S3-compatible endpoint or Push to your Splunk/Datadog.

Next steps (concrete):
- Connor will produce a 1-page sizing diagram + table (ETA: 48 hours).
- Karthik will run quick quantization experiments on your representative prompts (need a sanitized sample dataset; optional obfuscation).
- Hannah to coordinate a private-demo week of Feb 20 (we'll propose Wed/Thu currently).

Attachments: I attached a short "quantization tradeoffs" note (redwood-quantization-proposal.pdf) and an example arch sketch (current-arch-diagram.png).

If this aligns we'll prepare a short private demo environment and a canary plan for the burst window.

Cheers,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: redwood-quantization-proposal.pdf, current-arch-diagram.png
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 13:20:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: SparrowPay follow-ups (sizing & experiment plan)

Quick internal note before we send the sizing doc to SparrowPay:
- I'll run the quantization experiments on their sanitized prompt set as soon as Hannah confirms receipt (asking Priya for obfuscated examples is fine). Expect 24–36 hour turnaround.
- For the sizing diagram I'll include two cost/perf options: (A) mid-tier GPUs with 8-bit quant (lower cost, simpler infra), (B) high-perf GPUs with fewer replicas (lower latency headroom but higher per-hour cost).
- Risk item: if their requests >256 tokens become part of SLA, we need a separate plan (longer context = memory pressure => different kernel selection). Flagging for Connor to include a short note in the deck.

I'll draft the experiment README and link to the result notebook in the follow-up. Connor, want me to include microbench numbers (latency per token) or keep it higher level?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Applied ML / Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference
